answer: I'd like to talk about something I lost a couple of years ago, which still bothers me a little when I think about it. Something important I once lost was a small notebook in which I had jotted down ideas and personal reflections for over a year. It was a plain brown notebook, but it held everything from favourite quotations to plans for my career and thoughts about studying abroad. I must have left it somewhere while travelling, and by the time I realised, it was gone. I was coming back from Dhaka on a crowded bus after visiting my sister, and I think it slipped out of my bag when I [[dozed off]]. I was genuinely [[distraught]], because its contents were irreplaceable and deeply personal. I retraced my steps and asked around, but sadly it never turned up. I even phoned the bus company and went back to the ticket counter the next day, but nobody had handed anything in. For days I felt a real [[sense of loss]], almost as though I had lost a part of myself. What upset me most was that no amount of money could recover what was written inside. Eventually I had to [[come to terms with]] the fact that it was gone and try to move on. The experience taught me a valuable lesson about backing things up and being more careful with things that matter. These days I keep my notes on my laptop as well as on paper. Honestly, it still stings a little when I think about it. It made me realise how [[attached]] we can become to seemingly ordinary objects, simply because of what they represent to us.

followUps.q: Are you generally a careful person with your belongings?
followUps.answer: Much more careful now than I used to be. After losing that notebook, I always double-check my bag before getting off a bus, and I keep important things in one zipped pocket.

followUps.q: Have you ever found something that someone else lost?
followUps.answer: Yes, once I found a wallet on a rickshaw seat. I [[tracked the owner down]] using a card inside it, and he was so relieved that he insisted on buying me a cup of tea.

note: Replaced plain marks 'loss' and 'accept' with 'sense of loss' and 'come to terms with'; set the loss on a bus from Dhaka; added what he did (called the bus company); new mark 'dozed off'.
